players.name: Jimmy Neesham
players.didyouKnow: He scored centuries in his first two Test matches.
players.bio:
A promising allrounder, James Neesham made his one-day international debut against South Africa in early 2013.

His first 14 ODI matches included a high score of 42no and best bowling figures of 4-42. 

His made his Test debut against India in February 2014, scoring his maiden century in that match. He followed that performance with a second century in his second Test match, becoming the first New Zealander to score hundreds in his first two matches.

players.name: Matt Henry
players.didyouKnow: His 4-38 in his ODI debut was the third-best first-up performance by a Black Cap.
players.bio:
Matt Henry’s big chance for New Zealand came in January 2014. Included in the squad for the one-day international series against India, Henry was handed his Black Caps debut after an injury to teammate Hamish Bennett.

The right-arm fast-medium bowler grasped the opportunity with both hands, taking 4-38, the third-best figures on debut by a New Zealand player.

Henry made his second ODI appearance against South Africa in Hamilton in October 2014, taking 2-40. He originally missed out on a spot in the World Cup 2015 squad but was called up during the tournament after an injury to Adam Milne. 

He has yet to make his Test debut was impressed enough with his domestic form in 2014-15 to be included in the squad to tour England.

players.name: Hardik Pandya
players.bio:
Hardik Pandya made his international debut for India against Australia in 2016.

His ODI debut came later that year against New Zealand, while he made his Test debut in 2017 against Sri Lanka where he made a half-century in his first innings.

players.name: Axar Patel
players.didyouKnow: He wanted to be an engineer before his father encouraged him to play competitive cricket.
players.bio:
Not many people had heard of Akshar Patel before the 2014 Indian Premier League when the allrounder impressed for Kings XI Punjab with 17 wickets and was named emerging player of the tournament.

That performance brought the off-spinner to the attention of national selectors and Patel made his one-day international debut against Bangladesh in June 2014.

Patel, made his competitive debut in early 2012 playing for his home state Gujarat and was one of the key players in India under-23's title win in the ACC Emerging Teams Cup 2013.

Patel played a crucial hand in the 2024 T20 World Cup final against South Africa, hitting four sixes in his quickfire innings of 47 off 31, helping India win their first senior ICC tournament in over a decade.

players.name: Jasprit Bumrah
players.didyouKnow: On Boxing Day 2018, Bumrah became the first Asian bowler to take five wickets in Australia, England and South Africa in the same calendar year.
players.bio:
Jasprit Bumrah is on all levels a unique bowler. With a lackadaisical approach to the wicket, sometimes off no more than six paces, Bumrah is renowned as one of the most lethal fast bowlers across formats.

Bumrah emerged in Australia in 2016 as a limited-overs talent making both his ODI and T20I debuts against Australia within the space of four days.

He was an immediate success, and after years of great results with Mumbai Indians in the IPL, the longest format beckoned for Bumrah.

After Steve Smith (ODI) and David Warner (T20) were his first wickets in white-ball internationals, he claimed the scalp of AB de Villiers for his first Test wicket in January 2018 and took another 47 more wickets in the year to come.

He followed that up with a memorable 2018-19 summer against Australia, taking career-best figures of 6-33 in the Boxing Day Test as India won the Border-Gavaskar Trophy on Aussie soil.


He became the first bowler from an Asian nation to take five-wicket hauls in Australia, England and South Africa in the same year.


In 2022 Bumrah captained India in the fifth Test against England, finishing that campaign as player of the series with 23 wickets.

The unorthodox bowler was massive during India’s 2023 ODI World Cup run and 2024 T20 World Cup success, named player of the series in the latter for his 15 wickets at 8.26 and 2-18 in the final.

players.name: Arshdeep Singh
players.bio:
Arshdeep Singh made his international debut in a T20I against England in 2022.

The left-arm quick has been used as a white-ball specialist by India, with his speed and ability to consistently hit the yorker length deployed to good effect in the death overs regularly.

Arshdeep made a mark on the international stage instantly, achieving the rare feat of starting with a maiden over in his first-ever match.

He has since gone on to become first and the fastest Indian bowler to take 100 wickets in Men's T20Is.

A highlight of Arshdeep's career came at the MCG in 2022. Playing his first T20 World Cup game, a high-pressure encounter against arch-rivals Pakistan, the young fast bowler removed opposition captain Babar Azam on a golden duck with his very first ball. He followed it up with the wicket of the other opener, Mohammad Rizwan, in his next over.

The Punjab player finished as the leading wicket-taker for his team in that tournament. In the next edition of the T20 World Cup in 2024, he was the overall join-highest wicket taker for the tournament, taking 17 scalps. He was also named in the ICC Team of the Tournament.

Arshdeep is currently India's highest wicket-taker in Men’s T20Is, having overtaken Yuzvendra Chahal in 2025.
